h08.

Two types declare `RunOnce`, both named `Runner` but in different packages:

**`*s3presign.Runner` — invoked? Yes — `server/server.go:163` (`Server.startBackgroundRunners`), plus internally at `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:36` (`Runner.Run`'s ticker loop)**

Declared at `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:43`; it simply delegates to `CheckAndPresign`. The production entry point is `Server.startBackgroundRunners`, which constructs the runner via `s3presign.NewRunner(s.Store)` and calls `RunOnce(ctx)` synchronously for an immediate presign pass before spawning the goroutine that runs the 12-hour ticker loop.

**`*memopayload.Runner` — invoked? No — no caller anywhere**

Declared at `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:27`. Nothing references `memopayload.Runner`, `memopayload.NewRunner`, or this `RunOnce` — not from production code and not from tests. The only thing used out of that package is the free function `RebuildMemoPayload`, called from `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108` (memo creation) and `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:447` (memo update when content changes). So the type, its constructor, and its `RunOnce` method are currently dead code; the batch-rebuild-all-memos path it implements is never triggered.

No interface in the repo declares `RunOnce`, so these are the only two declarers — the grep for the identifier returns exactly the five hits above across all Go and TypeScript sources.
